title: REALISTA: Realistic Latent Adversarial Attacks that Elicit LLM Hallucinations
claim: Perturbing a prompt's latent code along a few valid edit directions, then decoding, yields a coherent, equivalent prompt that still triggers failure.
layout: 2 panels, latent-space geometry left, prompt boxes right, dotted encoder/decoder arrows
description: The left panel is a pale blue square labeled "Latent Space". The original latent point z0 sits at the top. Two gray arrows leave it, labeled δ1 z_academic and δ2 z_conditional. Dashed lines complete a parallelogram. A blue arrow from z0 ends at a gold point z, the sum of the two edits. On the right, a gray rounded box holds the original prompt x0, "What is the primary purpose of regularization in statistical learning?". A gold box below holds the attack prompt x, a rephrased version of the question. A dotted gray arrow labeled φ runs from the original prompt to z0. A dotted gold arrow labeled ψ runs from z to the attack prompt. Gray stands for the original and gold for the adversarial output. The eye goes first to the vector diagram, then to the two prompt boxes.
caption: Illustrative example of attack generation in \frameworknameabbr. Starting from the original prompt $\bm x_0$, the encoder $\phi$ maps it to its latent representation $\bm z_0$. A perturbation composed from edit directions is added to obtain $\bm z$, which is then decoded by $\psi$ back into the prompt space. The resulting adversarial prompt $\bm x$ remains semantically coherent and semantically equivalent to the original $\bm x_0$, while inducing a hallucination. See \mysecref{sec:realista} for the detailed construction process and Appendix \mysecref{app:our_attack_ex} for representative examples.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance across many tasks but remain vulnerable to hallucinations, making it important to systematically evaluate their reliability under realistic adversarial inputs. We formulate hallucination elicitation as a constrained optimization problem, where the goal is to find semantically coherent adversarial prompts that are equivalent to benign user prompts. Existing attack methods remain limited: discrete prompt-based attacks preserve semantic equivalence and coherence but search only over a limited set of prompt variations, while continuous latent-space attacks explore a richer space but often decode into prompts that are no longer valid rephrasings. To address these limitations, we propose REALISTA, a realistic latent-space attack framework. REALISTA constructs an input-dependent dictionary of valid editing directions, each corresponding to a semantically equivalent and coherent rephrasing, and optimizes continuous combinations of these directions in latent space. This design combines the optimization flexibility of continuous attacks with the semantic realism of discrete rephrasing-based attacks. Experiments demonstrate that REALISTA achieves superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art realistic attacks on open-source LLMs and, crucially, succeeds in attacking large reasoning models under free-form response settings, where prior realistic attacks fail. Code is available at https://github.com/Buyun-Liang/REALISTA.
